questions.subject: science
questions.content: What pulls objects toward the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the force that pulls objects toward the center of Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What helps a car stop when you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: Friction between the brake pads and wheels slows down and stops the car.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Ice is the ___ state of water.
questions.explanation: Ice is water in its solid state, with a fixed shape.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Steam is water in ___ form.
questions.explanation: Steam is water vapor, which is the gaseous form of water.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: In a food chain, plants are called ___ because they make their own food.
questions.explanation: Producers like plants make their own food through photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Lions are ___ in a food chain because they eat other animals.
questions.explanation: Consumers are animals that eat other organisms for energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which organ breaks down food into nutrients your body can use?
questions.explanation: The stomach uses acid and muscle movements to break down food.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: We breathe in ___ and breathe out carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: Our lungs take in oxygen from the air and release carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What provides electrical power in a simple circuit?
questions.explanation: A battery stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What happens to a light bulb when you close a switch in a circuit?
questions.explanation: Closing the switch completes the circuit, allowing electricity to flow and light the bulb.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which of the following are types of force? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Gravity, friction, and magnetism are all forces. Color is a property of light.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which are the three main states of matter? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Solid, liquid, and gas are the three main states of matter.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which animals are consumers? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Rabbits and tigers are consumers. Grass and trees are producers.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which organs are part of the digestive system? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Stomach, intestines, and esophagus are digestive organs. The heart is part of the circulatory system.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Objects fall down when dropped because of ___.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls all objects toward the center of Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Rough surfaces create more ___ than smooth surfaces.
questions.explanation: Rough surfaces have more bumps that rub against each other, creating more friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Water becomes ice when it ___.
questions.explanation: Freezing is the process where liquid water turns into solid ice at 0 degrees Celsius.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Mushrooms are ___ because they break down dead plants and animals.
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: A complete circuit needs a power source, wires, and a ___.
questions.explanation: A load (like a light bulb or motor) uses the electrical energy in a circuit. (Also accept: light bulb/device/appliance)

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Gravity only works on Earth and does not exist on the Moon.
questions.explanation: Gravity exists everywhere in the universe, but it is weaker on the Moon than on Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Water can exist as ice, liquid water, and steam.
questions.explanation: Water can be solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam/water vapor).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The heart is part of the digestive system.
questions.explanation: The heart is part of the circulatory system, not the digestive system.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Name three things you can do to reduce friction between two surfaces.
questions.correct_answer: Sample answers: Use oil or lubricant, make the surfaces smoother, use wheels or rollers.
questions.explanation: Friction can be reduced by smoothing surfaces, adding lubricants, or using rolling instead of sliding.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What unit do we use to measure weight (the force of gravity on an object)?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force measured in Newtons (N). Kilograms measure mass.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Why do car tires have tread patterns?
options: B. To increase friction with the road
questions.explanation: Tread patterns increase friction between the tire and road, improving grip and safety.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the process called when a liquid becomes a gas?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when liquid water turns into water vapor (gas).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the process called when a gas becomes a liquid?
questions.explanation: Condensation is when water vapor cools down and turns back into liquid water.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What do producers need to make their own food?
options: B. Sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Producers use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make food through photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What would happen if there were no decomposers in an ecosystem?
options: B. Dead things would pile up
C. Animals would have more food
D. The air would be cleaner
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms. Without them, dead matter would accumulate.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Where does most digestion and nutrient absorption happen?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is where most nutrients from food are absorbed into the blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which organ do we use to breathe air into our body?
questions.explanation: The lungs take in oxygen from the air and release carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What happens to a circuit when a switch is opened?
questions.explanation: Opening the switch creates a gap in the circuit, stopping the flow of electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which surface would have the least friction?
questions.explanation: Ice is very smooth and slippery, so it produces very little friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which factors affect the amount of friction between two surfaces? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Rougher textures and greater weight (normal force) both increase friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which are examples of physical changes (not chemical changes)? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Melting and boiling are physical changes. Burning and rusting are chemical changes.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which organisms are producers? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Grass, trees, and flowers are plants that make their own food. Wolves are consumers.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which materials are good conductors of electricity? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Copper and aluminum are metals that conduct electricity well. Plastic and rubber are insulators.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The force that pulls objects toward the center of Earth is called ___.
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force between objects with mass, pulling them toward Earth's center.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Sand spread on ice makes the surface less slippery because it increases ___.
questions.explanation: Sand creates a rougher surface, increasing friction and making it easier to walk on ice.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: When water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, it turns into water ___.
questions.explanation: Boiling causes liquid water to change into water vapor, which is a gas.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The trachea (windpipe) carries air to the ___.
questions.explanation: The trachea connects the mouth/nose to the lungs, allowing air to pass through.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: In a series circuit, if one light bulb breaks, the other bulbs ___.
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, there is only one path for electricity. If one component breaks, the whole circuit stops.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Freezing is the process when a liquid turns into a solid.
questions.explanation: Freezing is when a liquid loses heat and becomes a solid, like water turning to ice.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The large intestine absorbs water from the remaining food waste.
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and forms solid waste (feces).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Plastic is a good conductor of electricity.
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator, not a conductor. It does not allow electricity to pass through easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Explain why we need friction when we walk. What would happen if there were no friction between our shoes and the ground?
questions.correct_answer: Sample: Friction between our shoes and the ground prevents us from slipping. Without friction, our feet would slide backward and we could not move forward.
questions.explanation: Friction provides the grip needed to push against the ground and move forward.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Describe this food chain: grass -> rabbit -> fox. What would happen to the fox population if all the rabbits disappeared?
questions.correct_answer: Sample: The foxes would lose their main food source. Their population would decrease because they would starve or have to find other food.
questions.explanation: Removing an intermediate species disrupts the food chain and affects predators that depend on it.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What would happen to your weight if you traveled to the Moon?
options: C. It would stay the same
questions.explanation: The Moon has less gravity than Earth, so you would weigh less, though your mass stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which type of friction is usually the strongest?
questions.explanation: Static friction (when objects are not moving) is typically stronger than kinetic (sliding/rolling) friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the process called when a solid turns directly into a gas without becoming a liquid first?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is when a solid changes directly to a gas, like dry ice turning into carbon dioxide gas.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: In a food web, what are animals called that eat both plants and animals?
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plant and animal matter. Humans and bears are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What substance in the stomach helps break down food into smaller pieces?
questions.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid which helps digest food and kill bacteria.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange happens called?
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny sacs in the lungs where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the function of a resistor in an electric circuit?
options: B. To reduce or control current flow
D. To turn the circuit on and off
questions.explanation: A resistor limits the flow of electric current, protecting components and controlling circuit behavior.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the force that opposes the motion of objects moving through air called?
questions.explanation: Air resistance (drag) is the force that slows down objects moving through the air.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: What is the main role of apex predators (top predators) in an ecosystem?
options: B. To control the population of other animals
questions.explanation: Top predators keep prey populations in check, maintaining balance in the ecosystem.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which gas is transported by red blood cells to all parts of the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin that binds to oxygen and carries it to body tissues.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which are examples of balanced forces? (Select all that apply)
options: A. A book resting on a table
C. A person standing still on the floor
questions.explanation: Balanced forces occur when there is no motion. A book on a table and a standing person have balanced forces.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which phase changes absorb heat energy from the surroundings? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Melting and evaporation are endothermic processes that absorb heat. Freezing and condensation release heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which are parts of the human respiratory system? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: All four are parts of the respiratory system. The diaphragm is a muscle that helps with breathing.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Which components can be found in a simple electric circuit? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: A simple circuit can include all of these: battery (power), switch (control), bulb (load), and wire (connection).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Mass is measured in kilograms, but weight is measured in ___.
questions.explanation: Weight is a force, so it is measured in Newtons (N). Mass is measured in kilograms (kg).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Lubricants like oil are used to ___ friction between moving machine parts.
questions.explanation: Oil creates a slippery layer between surfaces, reducing friction and wear.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid is called its ___ point.
questions.explanation: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid (e.g., ice melts at 0°C).

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Energy in an ecosystem flows from the sun to ___ and then to consumers.
questions.explanation: Producers (plants) capture solar energy through photosynthesis and pass it to consumers.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: If too much current flows through a wire, it may cause a short ___ or fire.
questions.explanation: A short circuit happens when current flows along an unintended path, bypassing the load.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Friction always slows things down, so it is always bad and should be eliminated.
questions.explanation: Friction is not always bad. We need friction to walk, write, and stop cars. It should be reduced only when necessary.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: The diaphragm is a muscle that helps us breathe by contracting and relaxing.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm contracts to pull air into the lungs and relaxes to push air out.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: All energy in an ecosystem originally comes from the sun.
questions.explanation: Almost all energy on Earth comes from the sun, captured by producers through photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.content: Design a simple circuit with two light bulbs connected so that if one bulb breaks, the other still works. Describe or draw how you would connect them.
questions.correct_answer: Sample: Connect the two bulbs in parallel. Each bulb has its own path from the battery. If one path breaks, the other path still allows electricity to flow.
questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, components are connected on separate branches, so one can fail without affecting the others.
